description_en: The three-tiered Kvālkhu Gaṇeśa Mandira houses a severely eroded image of Gaṇeśa in its sanctum. Residents of Kvālkhu Ṭola worship this Gaṇeśa as their local deity. Tall buildings surround the temple to its north and west, however, a narrow passage allowes the temple's circumambulation. The base of the temple is furnished with four corner timber posts and a thick masonry rear wall further supports the structure. The Gaṇeśa statue is raised on a stone plinth and sheltered by a brass-clad roof with a pinnacle and atoraṇathat is flanked by two metal flags. The carved wooden columns at the front of the temple create an open arcaded structure. Tthe three roofs are covered with copper sheets and supported by carved struts displaying various Hindu deities. Architecturally, the metal frill work on the eaves is of particular interest. The temple's pinnacle is made of gilt copper and is surmounted by a parasol.No inscription or any other document confirming the initial construction date of the temple could be found. In 2009, the temple was reconstructed after it was severely damaged during the reconstruction of an adjoining house. An inscription dated NS 971 (CE 1891) is attached to the wall of the nearby Kvālkhu Gaṇeśa Sataḥ (LAL4186) and informs readers that it was renovated by a Jośī family from Nhulchẽ Nani. The inscription states the location of the image of Gaṇeśa and contains one of the sentences used in the invocation of the deity. It shows that thesataḥis related to this Gaṇeśa Temple.AsPruscha(2015, 158) mentions, every Tuesday an Amātya family used to place a silver image of Gaṇeśa inside the temple. However, this tradition no longer exists in its full form; the image is placed in the temple only on Indrajātrā. Aphalcācombined with a private house stands in front of the temple and was also once a part of local traditions. Every Tuesday, people would sit in thephalcāand sing and chant to Gaṇeśa. However, the house owner put an end to this some years ago. Now, people chant to Gaṇeśa whilst sitting on thesataḥ(LAL4186) located close to the temple.
description_ne: क्वाल्खु टोलबाट नःबहीतिर लाग्ने बाटोको उत्तरपट्टि यो मन्दिर अवस्थित छ । गणेशको मूर्ति राखिएको भूमितल्ला ढोका नहाली बनाइएको छ । कवलको बीचमा गणेशको शिलाको मूर्ति छ जुन निकै खिइसकेको छ । मूर्तिलाई बीचमा पारी सानो शिखर शैलीको संरचना बनाइएको छ जसलाई पित्तलको पाताले मोडी सजाइएको छ । गणेशको मूर्ति अगाडि एक जोडा पित्तलका ध्वजा छन् भने मूर्ति माथि सानो र ठुलो गरी पित्तलका दुई तोरण देख्न सकिन्छ । मन्दिरको मोहोडा भाग बाहेकका अन्य तीन दिशामा अग्ला क्रंक्रिड भवनहरु बनेकाले मन्दिर चेपुवामा पर्न गई शोभा घटेको देखिन्छ ।मन्दिरमा यसको निर्माणबारे जानकारी पाउन सकिने कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । सन् २००९ मा  मन्दिर संगैको घर पुनःनिर्माणको लागि भत्काउने क्रममा मन्दिरमा क्षति पुग्न गई सोही समय मन्दिर पनि पुनःनिर्माण गरिएको हो । मन्दिरको नजिकै सतःको भित्तामा रहेको ने.सं. ९७१को एक शिलालेखमा न्हुलछेँननिका जोशी खलकले सतः जीर्णोद्धार गरेको उल्लेख छ । अभिलेखको शिरोभागमा गणेशको मूर्ति र स्तुति भएबाट यो सतः  यही गणेश मन्दिरसँग सम्बन्धित रही बनेको बुझिन्छ ।क्वाल्खु टोलबासीले यस गणेशलाई स्थानगणेशका रूपमा पूज्ने गर्छन् । प्रुस्चाले (2015: 158) उल्लेख गरे झैँ प्रत्यक मंगलवार एक अमात्य परिवारबाट चाँदीको गणेशमूर्ति प्रदर्शनमा राख्ने परम्परा थियो तर हाल इन्द्रजात्राको समयमा मात्र प्रदर्शनमा राख्ने गरिएको छ । मन्दिरको ठिक अगाडि एउटा फल्चा रहेको छ । व्यक्तिगत घरसँग गाभिएर बनेको उक्त फल्चामा प्रत्येक मंगलबार गणेशको भजन हुने गर्दथ्यो । फल्चा गाभिएको घरका घरधनीले फल्चामा भजन गर्न रोक लागाएपछि हाल मन्दिर सँगैको सतःमा भजन गर्ने गरिएको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Jita Lāla (grand son of Sundara Rāja Bhaṇḍārī/son of Suvānanda Lāla) and his wife Nānī donated a copperpatāḥto Gaṇeśa.

In 2009, a house attached to the temple was dismantled to be reconstructed. During this process, the temple was damaged. Śrī Kvālkhu Ṭola Sudhāra Samiti therefore began renovations of the temple in 2009. This was completed in 2010 CE.

historical_events.event_name: Donation of brass flags on either side of the main image of Gaṇeśa
historical_events.event_description: Two brass flags were donated and fixed on either side of Gaṇeśa.
Suvānanda replaced the tiled roofs of the temple with copper plates.
